ui_verification.method: ALL 9 tabs are now PRIMARY screenshot-verified from a player in-game screen recording (2014 Golf R, PI 589, 20s, extracted frame-by-frame via ffmpeg) plus an earlier still of the Alignment tab. Section names, slider lists, directional pole labels, displayed units, lock/gating banners, and the three-panel layout are all confirmed from the footage. Earlier FH6 web research is retained as corroboration only.

confidence_legend.fh6_single: 🟡 only from FH6 web sources, not seen in footage
confidence_legend.needs_ingame: ❌ still unconfirmed — e.g. absolute slider min/max endpoints (the UI shows the current value + pole labels but never prints the numeric end stops)

ui_verification.locale_note: Units captured are US/Imperial locale: tire pressure PSI, springs LB/IN, ride height IN. A metric locale would show BAR, kgf/mm, and cm respectively.
ui_verification.remaining_gaps: Only the ABSOLUTE numeric min/max of each slider remains unverified — the menu shows the current value and the Soft/Stiff (etc.) poles but not the end-stop numbers. Per-car ranges also vary by chassis. Everything else (structure, poles, units, gating) is now ✅.
ui_verification.lock_behavior: A tab whose required upgrade is not installed shows ALL its sliders with a padlock icon (non-adjustable) and a yellow banner in the Description panel reading 'UNLOCKED BY INSTALLING <PART> UPGRADES'. It is a padlock + banner, never the literal text 'N/A'. ✅ confirmed.

observed_build.note: This 589 build spent its PI on suspension (race springs/dampers + adjustable alignment & tire pressure) but has NOT installed race brakes, ARBs, differential, transmission, or aero — so those tabs are currently un-tunable. Tuning recommendations for locked tabs only apply AFTER installing the matching race part.

tabs_note: Verified FH6 tab bar (from footage). There is NO separate 'Ride Height' tab — ride height is a section inside the SPRINGS tab. ✅
ui_layout: Every tab: LEFT 'Performance' readout panel (Braking Distance 60-0/100-0, Lateral Gs 60/120 mph, Acceleration & Speed 0-60/0-100/Top Speed, Miscellaneous: Mech. Balance / Aero Balance / Aero Efficiency); CENTER sliders grouped under green section headers showing the two directional poles; RIGHT 'Description' panel for the focused slider. ✅ confirmed across all tabs.
tuning_order_note: Order is broadly agreed; gearing-last and tires-first are universal. This is the TUNING SEQUENCE (methodology), not the tab layout — ride height is set inside the Springs tab even though it is a distinct tuning step.

non_slider_tuning_fh6.note: Two FH6 grip levers are NOT Tune-tab sliders — they are selected in the parts/upgrade (Customization) menu:
non_slider_tuning_fh6.tire_width: Tire WIDTH is adjustable independently front/rear in millimeters. Widening the front is a cheap PI grip lever. ✅ FH6 (web) / not a Tune-tab slider.
non_slider_tuning_fh6.tire_compound: Compound (Stock, Sport, Slick, Semi-Slick, Rally, Offroad, Snow, Drift, Drag) is an upgrade choice, not a Tune slider. ✅ FH6 (web).

categories.label: Tire Pressure
categories.gating: Always tunable (no upgrade required — unlocked on the observed build).
categories.fh6_note: Section 'Tire Pressure' with poles Low ↔ High, unit PSI. Front + Rear sliders. Width & compound are parts-menu items.

variables.label: Front tire pressure
variables.range_note: PSI confirmed on screen; absolute end-stops not displayed

categories.principle: Lower pressure = larger contact patch, more grip. Higher = sharper response, lower grip ceiling. Target ~31-33 psi HOT (the in-game Description confirms: low psi maximises contact patch but too low overheats; high psi adds response but can cause sudden grip loss).

categories.label: Gearing
categories.gating: UNLOCKED BY INSTALLING SPORT OR RACE TRANSMISSION UPGRADES (verbatim in-game banner). Sport unlocks Final Drive; Race unlocks individual gears + up to 10 speeds.
categories.fh6_note: Section 'Forward Gears', poles Speed ↔ Acceleration. Sliders: Final Drive + one per gear (observed build = 6-speed: 1st-6th). A speed graph (RPM x1000, axis 3-7) vs (mph, axis 0-180) is shown bottom-right. LOCKED on the observed build.

variables.label: Final drive ratio
variables.range_note: right pole = Acceleration (higher final drive = shorter gears = more accel, less top speed — per in-game Description). Numeric end-stops not displayed.

variables.label: Individual gear ratios (1st..Nth; up to 10 with Race trans)
variables.range_note: observed car = 6-speed; numeric end-stops not displayed

categories.principle: Short gearing = faster accel, lower top speed. Set Final Drive so the top gear's line just reaches the end of the speed graph. Tune LAST, while driving — shorter for touge hairpins, longer for highway zones.

categories.label: Alignment
categories.gating: Camber/Toe/Caster unlocked on the observed build (adjustable suspension fitted).
categories.fh6_note: Sections: 'Camber' (poles Negative ↔ Positive), 'Toe' (poles In ↔ Out), 'Front Caster' (poles Low ↔ High). All in degrees.
categories.principle: Modest negative camber for cornering grip without killing straight-line braking (the in-game Description warns too much negative camber cuts straight-line braking & accel). Higher caster sharpens turn-in and self-centering.

categories.label: Anti-Roll Bars
categories.gating: UNLOCKED BY INSTALLING RACE FRONT ANTIROLL BAR UPGRADES (verbatim banner). Front and rear each need their Race ARB part. LOCKED on the observed build.
categories.fh6_note: Single section 'Antiroll Bars', poles Soft ↔ Stiff, unitless scale. Front + Rear sliders.

variables.label: Front ARB stiffness
variables.range_note: 1.00-65.00 scale per FH6 web sources; on-screen end-stops not displayed

categories.principle: Balances rotation. Stiffer front = more stable/less rotation; stiffer rear = more rotation. AWD hot hatch: softer front / stiffer rear to fight understeer.

categories.label: Springs (incl. Ride Height)
categories.gating: Race Springs (coilovers) unlock spring rate + ride height. Unlocked on the observed build.
categories.fh6_note: Section 'Springs' (poles Soft ↔ Stiff, unit LB/IN) + section 'Ride Height' (poles Low ↔ High, unit IN) — BOTH inside the Springs tab. No separate Ride Height tab, no bump-stop field.

variables.label: Front spring rate
variables.range_note: LB/IN (US locale); per-car range, end-stops not displayed

variables.label: Front ride height
variables.range_note: IN (US locale); per-car range. VERIFIED example: 2014 Golf R front slider = 6.9 (min) to 8.1 (max) in — confirms absolute end-stops ARE car-specific and this chassis rides high.

categories.principle: Stiffer springs for smooth road/circuit, softer for dirt compliance. Lower ride height = lower CG/more road grip; raise for dirt. The in-game Description notes softening front springs vs rear increases front grip / reduces understeer.

categories.label: Damping
categories.gating: Race Springs/Dampers unlock damping. Unlocked on the observed build.
categories.fh6_note: Section 'Rebound Stiffness' (F/R) + section 'Bump Stiffness' (F/R), both poles Soft ↔ Stiff. Unitless, one-decimal values.
categories.principle: Rebound controls extension speed (~1.5-2x bump as a start); bump controls compression. The observed build runs rebound > bump on both axles (F 13.2/8.3, R 9.4/5.9). Softer damping for rough/dirt surfaces.

categories.label: Aerodynamics / Downforce
categories.gating: UNLOCKED BY INSTALLING RACE FRONT BUMPER UPGRADES (front) / race rear wing (rear) — verbatim banner. LOCKED on the observed build.
categories.fh6_note: Section 'Downforce', poles Speed ↔ Cornering (NOT 'less/more'), Front + Rear sliders, part-gated. Aero Balance & Aero Efficiency are Performance-panel readouts (observed 0.52 / 0.848, shown even with stock aero). FH6 tip: target Aero Balance ~0.40-0.50.

variables.label: Front downforce
variables.range_note: poles confirmed Speed<->Cornering; unit not visible (locked) — FH6 web says kgf/lb; range car-specific

categories.principle: More downforce (toward Cornering) = more grip, lower top speed. Toward Speed = less drag/higher top end. In FH6 watch Aero Balance (~0.40-0.50) rather than just maxing front. Description confirms: lower Balance = more understeer, higher = more oversteer.

categories.label: Braking
categories.gating: UNLOCKED BY INSTALLING RACE BRAKE UPGRADES (verbatim banner). LOCKED on the observed build.
categories.fh6_note: Two 'Braking Force' sections: Balance (poles Rear ↔ Front — left is Rear, right is Front) and Pressure (poles Low ↔ High). Part-gated.

variables.label: Brake balance
variables.range_note: left pole Rear, right pole Front; numeric end-stops not displayed (locked). Description: forward bias = stability, rearward = more oversteer under braking

categories.principle: Forward balance = stable braking; rearward = more trail-braking rotation/oversteer. Lower pressure if locking up under ABS-off.

categories.label: Differential
categories.gating: UNLOCKED BY INSTALLING RACE OR SPORT DIFFERENTIAL UPGRADES (verbatim banner). LOCKED on the observed build.
categories.fh6_note: AWD layout (observed): THREE sections — 'Front' (Acceleration + Deceleration, poles Low ↔ High), 'Rear' (Acceleration + Deceleration, poles Low ↔ High), and 'CENTER' (Balance, poles Front ↔ Rear). RWD would show Rear only; FWD Front only. The Center Balance IS the '30/70 power split'.

variables.label: Rear acceleration lock
variables.range_note: RWD/AWD; baseline CONTESTED across FH6 web sources

variables.label: Center balance (Front ↔ Rear)
variables.range_note: AWD-only; right pole = Rear; '30/70 split' = ~70 toward Rear

categories.principle: 0% open, 100% locked. Accel lock = on-throttle coupling; decel lock = off-throttle/braking stability. Accel/decel baselines CONTESTED across FH6 web — road-tune. Center 70-80% rear is well-agreed for AWD. The in-game Description confirms higher Accel = locks more quickly under power.
